comment: Per-file ceilings on the worst stack frame clippy measures in that file.
Keyed by file, the same way the source-length ratchet budgets, because a
large_stack_frames primary span is not always a function signature and a
function name is therefore not a stable key.
This budget covers RE-ENTRANT paths only. Frame size alone is not the
hazard: a large frame in a command entry point is entered once. The frames
that overflow a worker stack are the ones a nested descent re-enters, and
on 2026-09-03 a census of main found 157 frames over 100000 bytes across 96
files, most of them command entry points that carry no such risk.
Add a file here only with evidence that it is re-entered on a nested
agent, tool, or sub-agent descent. Shrinkage is tightened with --write.

files.why: Nested tool dispatch. Re-entered once per nested tool call; the frame a deep sub-agent descent overflowed on in harn#7804.
The dispatch callee on that same chain, entered inside the frame above.
